chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He (peace be upon him) was asked about the prey of the falcon and the dog when they hunt, kill the prey, and eat from it: Do you eat from their remains or not? So he (peace be upon him) said: As for what the bird has killed, do not eat it unless you slaughter it; and as for what the dog kills, and you have mentioned the Name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, over it, then eat, even if it has eaten from it.

key_terms.صَيْدِ الْبَازِي: Prey of the falcon/bird of prey

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in ruling between eating prey caught by a falcon versus a dog in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between hunting with birds of prey (which require manual slaughter/dhakāh due to their lack of explicit Quranic mention) and hunting with dogs (explicitly permitted in the Quran provided Allah's name is recited). It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the ritual invocation (tasmiyah) as the key condition for validity, even if the animal consumes part of the prey, reflecting the principle of permissibility unless proven otherwise.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup>

was asked about the falcon and the dog when they both hunt and have killed its prey and eaten from it. Can one eat from its remains or not?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for what the bird has killed, so do not eat it, except if you purify (slaughter) it; and as for that the dog kills, and the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Mentioned over it, so eat, even if it has eaten from it’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah who has said the following: “About the case of a man’s sending a hunting dog, with the mention of the name of Allah, to catch a prey, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘He can use it (the catch) for food even if the dog kills it and has eaten thereof. If the dog is not trained already for hunting, but is trained at that hour, then is sent to catch and it did and ate thereof, the dog is still a trained dog. On the other hand different from hunting dogs is what leopards, hawks and similar animals hunt. You must not use it for food unless you arrive in time to slaughter it properly; Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, ‘Mukallabin’ (dogged, trained dogs), thus, what is different from dogs its hunting is not edible unless you arrive in time to slaughter it.’”
